$comment: Mach-O relocatable object (.o, MH_OBJECT) for x86_64 macOS / Darwin. Third shipped object-format JSON (plan 14 LK3, 2026-05-30). Consumed by `src/link/format/macho.cpp` via the format-blind linker engine. mach_header_64 + section_64 + nlist_64 + relocation_info field values follow Apple's OS X ABI Mach-O File Format Reference + `<mach-o/loader.h>` / `<mach-o/nlist.h>` / `<mach-o/x86_64/reloc.h>`.
$stackReserveUnsupportedReasonComment: D-SQLITE-PE64-FULL-TIER-STACK-DEPTH: this artifact form has NO image header field for a stack size (a relocatable object / static archive is an INPUT to a later link, not a loadable program), so a `stackReserve` / `--stack-reserve` request against it is REFUSED with an actionable remedy -- request the reserve on the build that produces the final EXECUTABLE image -- rather than silently dropped.
$externCallDispatchComment: D-FORMAT-MACHO-X86_64-STATICLIB-DECLARES-NO-EXTERN-CALL-DISPATCH (closed 2026-08-06): DIRECT-PLT, the same contract the arm64 MH_OBJECT sibling declares and for the same reason -- an extern FUNCTION call lowers into this relocatable object as a plain call (x86_64 `E8 disp32`) plus an X86_64_RELOC_BRANCH against an N_UNDF|N_EXT symbol carrying its REAL import name; the FINAL linker (ld64/clang) synthesizes the stub and __got, and DSS never builds a stub inside a `.o`. The arm64 sibling's comment used to say the x86_64 object 'stays leaf-only ... its walker code is shared and lights up by declaring this field when a runner lands' -- the runner landed (the operator's Mac runs the macho64-x86_64 leg under Rosetta, declared in real-examples/c/sqlite/legs.json) and this is that declaration. THE CONSEQUENCE OF THE ABSENCE WAS MEASURED, NOT INFERRED: before this key existed, a two-line TU whose only extern is `puts` failed at MIR->LIR with `error[L_RequiredLirOpcodeMissing] ... module declares extern imports but the active object format declares no externCallDispatch shape`, on THIS format and on `-staticlib`, while both arm64 siblings compiled the identical source at rc=0. `indirect-slot` would be WRONG here and the distinction is not cosmetic: it is the PE IAT / load-time-bound-slot shape, and using it in a Mach-O relocatable would deref the stub's own CODE bytes as a function pointer. Value NOT copied from the arm64 file: the shape is a property of the OBJECT FORMAT's link contract, which is why both arches answer `direct-plt` and why the `-exec` and `-dylib` x86_64 siblings already did.
$weakDefinitionComment: D-CONFIG-WEAK-DEFINITION-DIALECT-NOT-DECLARED + D-LK-WEAK-DEFINITION-DIALECT-UNCONSULTED-BY-ELF-AND-MACHO-WRITERS: HOW this format spells a WEAK DEFINITION -- a symbol several translation units may define, of which the linker keeps one. Mach-O puts the weakness in a per-symbol FLAG BIT set ALONGSIDE an ordinary binding: N_WEAK_DEF (0x0080) in the nlist_64's n_desc, on a symbol that is otherwise N_SECT|N_EXT -- the constant re-verified against MacOSX.sdk/usr/include/mach-o/nlist.h. That is exactly what distinguishes `symbol-flag` from ELF's `symbol-binding` (where the weakness IS the binding value) and from COFF's `comdat` (a per-SECTION policy). Written by `definedNDesc` in the MH_OBJECT arm of src/link/format/macho.cpp. THE IMAGE SIBLINGS (exec / dylib) DELIBERATELY DECLARE NO DIALECT, AND THAT IS AN ANSWER RATHER THAN AN OMISSION: their walker encodes no weak definition at all -- refuseWeakImageAlias refuses one outright, because N_WEAK_DEF on an IMAGE additionally needs MH_WEAK_DEFINES in the mach header and those writers copy the schema's flags verbatim (D-LK3-DYLIB-WEAK-EXPORT) -- and a key nobody reads drifts silently while reading as authoritative, which is worse than no key at all. THIS IS A DIALECT ROW, NOT A CAPABILITY FLAG: it says how this format spells something it CAN express, never that it cannot -- see D-LK-PE-ALTERNATENAME-DECLARE-AND-REFUSE for why an implementation gap recorded as a format incapability is a false fact in the place most likely to be trusted later. The MH_OBJECT arm READS this key and refuses loud on a dialect it has no encoder for, so the declaration cannot drift away from what is actually emitted. The loader additionally refuses this key at LOAD when the declared dialect is not one the resolved backend's walker writes (ObjectFormatBackend::weakDefinitionDialects).
$dataModelComment: FC3 c1: 64-bit linux/darwin are LP64 (int 32, long 64, ptr 64). Consumed by the semantic tier (buildCuMir threads format.dataModel() into analyze()): c long binds I64 here. REQUIRED closed-enum field; the loader rejects a missing or unknown value (a silent default would bake wrong widths).
$headerNameMatchingComment: D-PP-HEADER-CASE-INSENSITIVE-PE: macOS ships on APFS/HFS+ volumes that are CASE-INSENSITIVE by default (the installer default since 10.13; a case-sensitive volume is opt-in), and Apple's own SDK headers rely on it -- `<TargetConditionals.h>` / `<CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>` are routinely spelled with divergent case. REQUIRED closed-enum field. DSS ASCII-folds the comparison ITSELF per path component rather than delegating to fs::exists, so a Darwin cross-build from a case-sensitive Linux host resolves exactly as it does natively.
$cSymbolDecorationComment: D-FFI-CMANGLING-RULE-NOT-CONFIG-DRIVEN: Apple's C ABI prefixes EVERY C symbol with exactly ONE leading underscore, on both 32- and 64-bit Mach-O -- the rule has no bitness axis and no per-arch axis (the arm64 and x86_64 slices of the universal libSystem decorate identically), which is why it is declared per FORMAT and not per target. EVIDENCE, EACH LABELLED. MEASURED-BY-EXECUTION (recorded TF-C113, the macOS cross-build arc): a Windows host cross-emitted a mach-o arm64 binary whose only process-exit path is the `_exit` import, and it RAN on the operator's Apple Silicon Mac and exited correctly -- an undecorated `exit` would have been an unresolved dyld bind, not a cosmetic difference. MEASURED (recorded TF-C121): libSystem's x86_64 slice exports BOTH `_fstat` and `_fstat$INODE64`, i.e. the C identifier `fstat` reaches the linker as `_fstat`. NOT RE-MEASURED THIS CYCLE, stated rather than buried: the Mac is a personal machine and was not declared reachable, so nothing here rests on a probe taken today. This key is the single owner of a fact that previously had TWO: the closed C++ table `kCManglingRules` (src/ffi/mangling/c_mangle.cpp, keyed on ObjectFormatKind) and, redundantly, a literal encoding in the descriptors themselves -- the macho64-*-exec files spell `processExit.importMangledName` as `_exit` while their elf/pe siblings spell it `exit`. Two owners in two languages, with nothing forcing them to agree. RED-ON-DISABLE, stated precisely for the tier that exists today (MEASURED 2026-08-06 by actually removing the key from a shipped file and running the suite): DELETE this key and the format is REFUSED AT LOAD -- TWO errors at /cSymbolDecoration, one C_MissingField from the loader and one from ObjectFormatData::validate(), which loadFromText runs before returning -- so every test and example that loads this format goes red, naming the file. CHANGING the value is now an equally REAL lever, and this sentence was corrected the moment it became true: before step C4 the engine still read a C++ table and the value here changed no emitted binary. C4 landed (same cycle, TF-C122), and the effect is MEASURED 2026-08-06 -- flipping macho64-arm64-darwin-exec from `leading-underscore` to `none` and RECOMPILING NOTHING made the engine emit `printf` where it had emitted `_printf`, reddening tests/ffi/test_c_mangle.cpp's SchemeIsReadFromTheShippedSchemaNotACppTable. That is the whole point of the anchor: the answer lives in this file, so editing this file changes what the compiler emits. Two further pins guard the value: tests/link/test_c_symbol_decoration.cpp asserts the per-kind answer across all 24 shipped files and cross-checks it against this family's own processExit.importMangledName.
$cCallingConventionComment: D-FFI-ABI-CATALOG-SELECTS-CALLING-CONVENTION-BY-FORMAT-IDENTITY: the platform C ABI for code compiled into this format, NAMING a row in the paired target's callingConventions[] array. This selection used to be re-derived in C++ by `kAbiCatalog`, a closed table keyed on (target name, ObjectFormatKind) — while this very string was already written here. Two owners of one fact; the table is deleted and this is the single owner. System V AMD64 (`rdi,rsi,rdx,rcx,r8,r9`).
$outputExtensionComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: the extension the driver appends to an artifact this format produces. This used to be derived in C++ by `program/target_spec.cpp::outputExtensionFor`, a five-arm `switch (fmt.kind())` with a NESTED per-flavor switch inside each arm -- seven identity mentions computing a NAMING fact, which is not an engine behaviour at all. The nest existed because one ObjectFormatKind spans several artifact flavors; a DOCUMENT is exactly one flavor, so the whole derivation collapses to this one string. REQUIRED on every format. An EMPTY value is a DECLARED answer and not an omission -- a Unix executable carries no extension -- which is why the in-memory field is an `optional` and the loader's required check asks `contains`, never `empty`.
$archiveFlavorComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: WHICH `ar` variant this format's ECOSYSTEM uses. Declared on every native format, not only the `container: archive` ones, because that is what the deleted C++ derivation answered: `(format.kind() == ObjectFormatKind::Pe) ? Coff : SysV` was handed WHATEVER format the caller had, and `linkAndWriteStaticArchive` is reachable with the RELOCATABLE format of an ecosystem as well as its archive one (MEASURED -- restricting the key to archives reddened link/test_ar_writer and program/test_static_link). NOT cosmetic: the coff flavor carries the little-endian second linker member link.exe requires to resolve members at all. A closed VERB rather than an open name, because an archive layout is an ENGINE capability -- only variants `writeArArchive` realizes can be honored.
$targetArchComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: the .target.json NAME this format is for. `crossValidateTargetFormat` compares it against TargetSchema::name() -- two DECLARED NAMES -- where it used to run a six-arm `switch (format.kind())` reading a DIFFERENT field per identity (elf.machine / pe.machine / macho.cputype) and compare each against a hardcoded C++ table, kTargetArchMachineCodes, keyed on (target name x format kind). THAT TABLE IS DELETED, and the argument is ONE OWNER rather than tidiness: `arm64 is EM_AARCH64 = 183` had two owners -- this document's own machine field and that C++ row -- with nothing forcing them to agree, which is the identical shape as kCManglingRules and kAbiCatalog. The number now lives only in the document that emits it, and the pairing question is answered by a name this document states outright. Adding a new arch is now JSON-ONLY.
$predefinedMacrosComment: TF-C97 (D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): the C-visible face of this file's `dataModel` above, DERIVED FROM THAT VALUE AND NEVER FROM THIS FILE'S NAME -- the loader synthesizes no macro name and the engine performs no format-identity branch; it merges whatever rows are declared here with the language's `preprocess.predefinedMacros` and the target's `predefinedMacros`, applying `availableObjectFormats` exactly once. DECLARED ON THE FORMAT because the data model is per-(OS x format), not per-CPU: the same x86_64 target is LP64 here and LLP64 under pe64-x86_64-windows-*, so a target-side row would be wrong on one of its own formats -- which is exactly what both .target.json files say when they record `__LP64__`/`_LP64` as DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED and defer to the format. BOTH spellings, each value 1: MEASURED 2026-07-30 with `/usr/bin/clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target <triple>` (Apple clang 21.0.0), __LP64__ and _LP64 are BOTH defined as 1 on arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-linux-gnu and x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, and NEITHER is defined on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. COLLISION POLICY: a name declared by this file AND the language or target config is FATAL (C_ConflictingPredefinedMacro) -- no side silently wins. WHAT IT UNBLOCKS, MEASURED: the macOS SDK gates 234 occurrences across 91 headers on __LP64__, so without these rows DSS compiled the SDK's ILP32 arms while its own widths were LP64 (sizeof(long)==8), and $SDK/usr/include/mach/port.h:113-114 then asserted the user32 struct size 12 instead of user64's 16 -- sqlite mem1.c's three error[S0029]. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete this key and examples/c/predefined_lp64_macho stops exiting 42.
$bitFieldStrategyComment: D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD-ABI-EXACT: macOS/Darwin (Apple x86_64 + arm64) uses the generic LSB-first bit-field allocation. Apple's enumerated arm64 ABI divergences from generic AAPCS64 are char/wchar_t signedness, long double=double, va_list, the red zone, the stack argument area, and empty-struct handling — NOT bit-field packing — so Mach-O shares gnu_packed. Byte-ABI-exact to clang, confirmed by the macOS CI cross-compile-compare leg (the only runtime witness for Apple).
$longDoubleFormatComment: FC17.9(e) D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE: macOS x86_64 `long double` = x87 80-bit, 16/16 (SysV). See macho64-x86_64-darwin-exec.
$supportedDataSectionsComment: D-CONFIG-MACHO-X86_64-DARWIN-SUPPORTED-DATA-SECTIONS-ABSENT (closed 2026-08-06) — the last two cells of that anchor are this file and its `-staticlib` sibling, which until now declared `text` and nothing else while every arm64 macho format and the x86_64 `-exec`/`-dylib` siblings declared a set. ★ TWO KEYS, ONE CHANGE, AND SPLITTING THEM IS THE HAZARD THE ANCHOR NAMES: the linker's PRE-WALKER gate reads THIS set (`acceptsDataSection` — a generic set-membership with zero format-name branches, the same field ELF and PE declare), and the `sections[]` rows below tell the WALKER where each kind lands. Declaring one without the other is not a half-fix but a WORSE diagnostic — MEASURED on the `-exec` sibling 2026-08-05, opting into `rodata` with no row leaves `encodeExecDynamic`'s `hasConst && secConst == nullptr` guard a bare `return {}` and the caller reports a generic `K_ImageEmpty` that never names the cause. ⓘ THE MH_OBJECT ARM IS NOT THAT ARM, and that was MEASURED here rather than inherited: this walker routes every PRESENT kind through `requireSection`, so a declared-but-rowless kind fails loud naming the section (MEASURED 2026-08-06 by deleting the rodata row from this file with the opt-in left in place, quoted VERBATIM: `error[K_NoMatchingObjectFormat] [target=x86_64:macho64-x86_64-darwin] Mach-O writer (MH_OBJECT) requires section kind 'rodata' but object format 'macho64-x86_64-darwin' does not declare one`). The pair still ships together — because the gate must not ADMIT what the walker cannot PLACE — but the reason is that invariant, not a fear that this arm would go quiet. ★ EVIDENCE, EACH AT ITS OWN GRADE. MEASURED on this host, end to end through the real CLI: one TU carrying a string literal (rodata), `int counter = 7;` (data), a tentative `int zero_global;` (bss) and two const-with-load-time-relocation globals (relro) compiled rc=1 with `error[K_NoMatchingObjectFormat] ... section=rodata ... does not advertise that section in its 'supportedDataSections' set` BEFORE this key, and rc=0 with the `.o` emitted AFTER — while `macho64-arm64-darwin` compiled the identical source at rc=0 throughout as the matched control. ⛔ NOT MEASURED, stated rather than buried: NOTHING RAN. A Mach-O `.o` is an INPUT to a later ld64 link, and no Mac was reachable from this host, so what is claimed is 'the walker places the bytes and the emitted object parses', never 'ld64 accepted it' and never 'it executed'. ★ NOT A BULK COPY OF THE arm64 SIBLING, and the difference is checkable rather than asserted: the SET is a property of what the MH_OBJECT walker can PLACE — shared format-blind code whose only per-cputype dispatch is the EXEC-only `__stubs` substrate a relocatable never emits — and Mach-O segment/section NAMES carry no arch axis, which this family's own x86_64 `-exec` file already states and ships. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT BROUGHT OVER: the arm64 `relocations[]` rows (this file keeps X86_64_RELOC_UNSIGNED_8/_4, and it is that abs64 row the relro/data pointer fixups resolve through), and `tdata`/`tbss` — the MH_OBJECT walker emits no TLV machinery on ANY arch and rejects a thread-local item loud (`K_FormatLacksThreadLocalSupport`), so declaring them would advertise a capability that does not exist. RED-ON-DISABLE, MEASURED 2026-08-06 by a fail-closed mutator (witness unique before / absent after, sha256 DIFFERS, mutant still parses, file restored and its sha256 re-verified): delete this key and the probe above returns to `error[K_NoMatchingObjectFormat] ... section=rodata`, and BOTH pins red naming this file — `ObjectFormatFamilySymmetry.EveryMachoFormatDeclaresItsDataSectionsWithTheirRows` (tests/link, the declaration) and `Program_CompileFiles.MachORelocatableTiersPlaceEveryDeclaredDataSection` (tests/program, the emission: source through the real pipeline, then the emitted section_64 table parsed by a reader that shares no code with DSS, on all four relocatable Darwin arms). Delete the rodata `sections[]` row INSTEAD and both red again with the walker's own message — which is the point of pinning the pair rather than the key.

macho.$comment: mach_header_64 identity. cputype = CPU_TYPE_X86_64 (0x01000007 — CPU_ARCH_ABI64 bit OR'd with x86 ABI type 7). cpusubtype = CPU_SUBTYPE_X86_64_ALL (3). filetype = MH_OBJECT (1). flags = 8192 = MH_SUBSECTIONS_VIA_SYMBOLS (0x2000), SET 2026-08-20 — see below; this ONE NUMBER is the whole switch and the whole revert. ★ IT IS THE HEADER HALF OF A PAIR, AND THE PAIR IS THE ONLY DISCRIMINATOR MACH-O HAS between a whole file-local (`static`) body and an interior block label: nlist_64 carries no size field, so DSS emitted both as a bare N_SECT with n_desc = 0 and no reader could tell them apart — the archive-member reader classified every `static` function as a label and DROPPED ITS BYTES, loudly when it was called and SILENTLY when it was not (D-LINK-NONEXTERNAL-DEFINED-SYMBOL-READ-AS-BLOCK-LABEL-NOT-ATOM). The per-symbol half is N_ALT_ENTRY (n_desc bit 0x0200), which the writer now stamps on the synthetic per-block labels; this flag is the producer's declaration that every OTHER defined symbol starts an atom of its own. This is the FORMAT's vocabulary, not a DSS convention: ✔MEASURED (operator, real Apple Silicon, 2026-08-20) `/usr/bin/clang -c -O0` sets 0x00002000 on EVERY ordinary `.o`, and ✔MEASURED (this cycle, clang 19 targeting arm64-apple-macos) the same, so an object WITHOUT the flag is the odd one out and cannot be sliced symbol-by-symbol by anyone. ⚠ THE PRIOR TEXT HERE WAS TRUE WHEN WRITTEN AND IS NOW SATISFIED RATHER THAN OVERTURNED: it withheld the flag because the walker emitted a flat `__text` with 'no N_ALT_ENTRY subsection markers', so advertising it 'would lie to ld64 about function-granular dead-strip safety', and deferred the work to plan 14 §3.1 D-LK3-2 — an anchor that closed as the MH_EXECUTE/LC_MAIN row and so had owned this for nobody. The markers now exist; the declaration is honest. ⚠ THE BIT IS A LICENCE, NOT A REQUEST: it permits Apple's ld64 to dead-strip at SYMBOL granularity in every artifact built from these objects, which is why it was gated on hardware evidence rather than on a DSS round trip. ✔MEASURED (operator, real Apple Silicon, 2026-08-20): 38 DSS mach-o objects linked by ld64 under `-dead_strip` with the flag patched ON vs OFF — 38/38 rc=0 both ways, 38/38 ran identically; and a four-variant table (flag on/off × N_ALT_ENTRY on/off), each linked with and without `-dead_strip` — all 8 cells rc=0 with identical correct output. ★ NO C++ READS THIS VALUE: the writer copies `MachOIdentity::flags` verbatim into the header, and the reader asks only whether the bit is present in the object it is READING. So if a widened ld64 sweep ever shows a behaviour change, setting this number back to 0 is the entire rollback — the N_ALT_ENTRY markers stay honest and the reader falls back to its narrower external-only rule with the coverage guard still refusing any dropped body.

$buildVersionComment: D-LK10-ENTRY-MACHO-EXIT, MH_OBJECT arm: LC_BUILD_VERSION in a RELOCATABLE object. ★ `image.*` here means THIS MACH-O FILE -- not 'a loadable image'. MH_OBJECT is a `filetype` exactly like MH_EXECUTE, and `build_version_command` is legal in both, which is why the key needs no new vocabulary to reach a `.o`. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-13 on the operator's Apple Silicon Mac (macOS 26.5.2, Apple clang, `ld` PROJECT:ld-1267): `clang -c` emits into a plain `.o`, IN THIS ORDER, LC_SEGMENT_64 / LC_BUILD_VERSION (cmdsize 24, platform 1 = PLATFORM_MACOS, ntools 0) / LC_SYMTAB / LC_DYSYMTAB. Without the key ld64 prints `ld: warning: no platform load command found in '<tu>.o', assuming: macOS` once per object -- fidelity + noise, not breakage, but a per-object warning trains readers to ignore linker warnings and can bury a real one. THE PLATFORM IS PER-OS, NOT PER-CPU, which is why this x86_64 sibling declares the identical `macos` / 11.0 / 11.0 the arm64 object and both darwin -exec formats declare; the cputype above is the only axis that differs. ⚠ NOT RE-MEASURED FOR THIS SLICE: the reachable Mac is Apple Silicon, so the ld64 observation was taken on arm64 objects. Stated rather than buried -- the load command's wire shape and ld64's platform rule carry no cputype axis (both darwin -exec formats already share the identical block), so nothing here rests on an x86_64-specific probe. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete this block and mach_header_64 ncmds falls 3 -> 2, sizeofcmds drops 24, and the byte pins in tests/link/test_macho_writer.cpp go red.

sections.$comment: Executable code. Mach-O two-level naming: section `__text` inside segment `__TEXT`. section_64.flags = S_REGULAR (0x0) | S_ATTR_PURE_INSTRUCTIONS (0x80000000) | S_ATTR_SOME_INSTRUCTIONS (0x00000400) = 0x80000400. addrAlign = 16 RAW BYTES (x86_64/arm64 code alignment). section_64.align is a LOG2 exponent and the walker converts (std::countr_zero), exactly as every other section row here is converted; this row used to carry the literal log2 4 and be written VERBATIM, which made one schema key mean two different things across the object and exec families (D-MACHO-TEXT-SECTION-ALIGN-RAW-BYTES-INTO-LOG2-FIELD). PE's substrate `type` field repurposed for Mach-O section_64.flags.
sections.name: __text

sections.$comment: D-CONFIG-MACHO-X86_64-DARWIN-SUPPORTED-DATA-SECTIONS-ABSENT: read-only initialized data — string literals and const globals carrying NO relocations — in section `__const` inside the R+X `__TEXT` segment, which is where clang places it in an x86_64 `.o`. section_64.flags (the substrate's `type` field) = S_REGULAR (0): no write attribute and no exec attribute, so folding it into __TEXT preserves W^X. ★ addrAlign 8 is a RAW-BYTE FLOOR handed to the shared `buildExecDataSection` substrate — NOT the literal log2 the `__text` row above carries; the walker H1-raises it to the strictest member's alignment and writes section_64.align as that value's log2. The two conventions live in one array on purpose and this comment is the only thing that says so. No `virtualAddress` key: MH_OBJECT section addrs are walker-computed in the flat `.o` address space and validate() rejects a non-zero VA on an object row.
sections.name: __const

sections.$comment: Writable initialized globals (`int counter = 7;`) — clang's `__DATA,__data`, a segment distinct from the r-x `__TEXT` because a store into __TEXT faults. section_64.flags (`type`) = S_REGULAR (0). A reloc-bearing MUTABLE pointer global lands here too, and the walker emits this section's OWN relocation_info table for it — resolving the fixup through this file's `X86_64_RELOC_UNSIGNED_8` row (kind 2 = x86_64.target.json's `abs64`), which is precisely the axis that IS per-CPU: the arm64 sibling reaches the same place through ARM64_RELOC_UNSIGNED. addrAlign 8 = raw-byte floor (H1-raised, written as log2 — see the rodata row).
sections.name: __data

sections.$comment: D-LK-RELRO-CONST-DATA-RELOCATABLE (Mach-O x86_64 `.o` arm): a CONST global carrying LOAD-TIME relocations — `int *const p = &x;`, a const function-pointer table (sqlite's VFS method tables / `aSyscall[]`) — which clang emits as `__DATA,__const`, the `.o` PRECURSOR of the image's `__DATA_CONST,__const` (ld64 gathers these input sections into __DATA_CONST, read-only after rebase; the Mach-O analog of gcc's `.data.rel.ro`). ★ A DISTINCT ROW, NOT A FOLD — and that DIVERGES from this same family's `-exec`/`-dylib` files deliberately: those list `relro` in `supportedDataSections` with NO row of its own because the IMAGE walker merges a relro item into `__DATA,__data` and dyld rebases the slot, whereas the relocatable arm keeps the two apart so ld64 receives the input shape clang would have produced. The (segment, section) PAIR is the Mach-O identity, which is what makes (`__DATA`,`__const`) a different section from the (`__TEXT`,`__const`) rodata row above rather than a duplicate name. relocation_info has no addend column, so the addend is written INTO the 8-byte slot (Mach-O's in-place-addend convention) and the final linker computes S + A.
sections.name: __const

sections.$comment: Zero-initialized globals (tentative `int g;`) — clang's `__DATA,__bss`. section_64.flags (`type`) = S_ZEROFILL (1): the section has a size and a flat-space addr but NO file bytes (section_64.offset = 0), so the addr cursor advances while the file does not, and the walker emits it LAST per the Mach-O zerofill-last convention. addrAlign 8 = raw-byte floor (H1-raised, written as log2 — see the rodata row).
sections.name: __bss

sections.$comment: D-LK-MACHO-COMPACT-UNWIND-SECTION-REFUSED-BLOCKS-EVERY-STOCK-MACOS-ARCHIVE: PER-FUNCTION UNWIND METADATA -- the section Apple's clang emits BY DEFAULT, which is why its absence from this list refused every stock macOS `.a`. ★ THE VOCABULARY IS THE FIX, NOT A GUARD CHANGE: `readRelocatableObject` was right to refuse a section it could not classify, and the linker must never learn the NAME `__compact_unwind` -- it reads the universal `kind`, and the next platform's equivalent section is a row like this one rather than a second branch. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-24 against Apple clang 21.0.0 (macOS 26.5.2 arm64, `clang -c` with NO flags, `otool -l` + a decoder written from the format description): segment `__LD` / section `__compact_unwind`, section_64.flags (substrate `type`) = 0x02000000 = S_ATTR_DEBUG, section_64.align = 3 (log2) => addrAlign 8 raw-byte floor, and a body of 3 records for 3 functions in 0x60 bytes => entrySize 32 (`{ uint64 functionStart; uint32 length; uint32 encoding; uint64 personality; uint64 lsda; }`). entrySize is READ, not decoration: it is how the reader states HOW MANY function unwind descriptions an object carries without any record layout being hardcoded in C++. ⚠ `__LD` IS A LINKER-ONLY PSEUDO-SEGMENT -- no such segment exists in a linked image, so this row appears ONLY on the relocatable documents and never on an exec or dylib one. ⚠ THIS ROW MAKES DSS READ THE SECTION, NOT CARRY IT, AND THAT IS STILL TRUE OF **THIS** ROW ALONE. D-LK-MERGED-FOREIGN-FUNCTIONS-CARRY-NO-UNWIND-INFO-IN-THE-IMAGE: a compact record is `{fnStart, len, encoding, personality, lsda}` with NO PC DIMENSION, so it describes the frame in the function BODY only. Turning it into an FDE that claims the body rule holds from pcOffset 0 would manufacture an assertion clang never made and be WRONG for every prologue PC -- so it is NOT converted, and the reader says out loud, once per section, which functions reach the image undescribed. Its honest carry is a `__TEXT,__unwind_info` synthesis, which DSS does not yet emit. ★ THE `encoding` KEY IS WHAT LETS THIS ROW COEXIST WITH A SECOND `unwind` ROW: the ROLE (`kind`) is shared, the WIRE ENCODING is not, and the reader dispatches on the declared encoding rather than on this section's NAME. `entrySize` is meaningful HERE and only here -- a compact record is fixed-width, a DWARF CIE/FDE is not.
sections.name: __compact_unwind

sections.$comment: D-LK-MERGED-FOREIGN-FUNCTIONS-CARRY-NO-UNWIND-INFO-IN-THE-IMAGE: THE SECOND `unwind` ROW, IN A DIFFERENT WIRE ENCODING -- and the reason the section-row identity had to become the (kind, encoding) PAIR. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-25 on real Apple Silicon (macOS 26.5.2), `/usr/bin/cc -arch x86_64 -c foreign.c` with NO other flag: ONE x86_64 object carries BOTH `__LD,__compact_unwind` AND this section, while the arm64 object from the SAME compiler and the SAME source carries compact ONLY. section_64.flags (substrate `type`) = 0x6800000B = S_COALESCED (0x0B) | S_ATTR_NO_TOC (0x40000000) | S_ATTR_STRIP_STATIC_SYMS (0x20000000) | S_ATTR_LIVE_SUPPORT (0x08000000); section_64.align = 3 (log2) => addrAlign 8 raw-byte floor. ★ THIS ROW IS THE WHOLE MACH-O CARRY, AND IT ADDS NO EMIT PATH: DWARF CFI is the encoding `src/link/format/dwarf_cfi_decode.hpp` already inverts into the neutral `CfiFunction` vocabulary, and the Mach-O image writer already builds `__TEXT,__eh_frame` from that -- so declaring the row is what makes a merged foreign function's unwind description reach the image. ⚠ `entrySize` IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT (0): a DWARF CIE/FDE is VARIABLE-LENGTH, so a record count computed from a fixed width would be a lie, and the reader must never divide this body by anything. Its compact sibling carries 32 because a compact record really is fixed-width -- the two rows disagreeing about that field is the field being READ rather than copied. ⚠ NO `virtualAddress` key: MH_OBJECT section addrs are walker-computed in the flat `.o` address space and validate() rejects a non-zero VA on an object row. ⚠ RELOCATABLE DOCUMENTS ONLY -- the IMAGE-side `__TEXT,__eh_frame` is SYNTHESIZED by the Mach-O writer from `CfiFunction`, never named through this table, which is why the -exec and -dylib documents list no unwind row at all.
sections.name: __eh_frame

sections.$comment: D-LK-OBJECT-CARRIES-NO-SUMMARY-OR-MIR-SECTION. The per-module LINK-TIME-OPTIMIZATION SUMMARY. flags = S_ATTR_DEBUG (0x02000000 = 33554432), which is Mach-O's spelling of non-ALLOC: it is a LINKER INSTRUCTION -- do not load these bytes into the image -- and it is the SAME value the `__LD,__compact_unwind` row already carries for the same reason, reused rather than re-decided. ⚠ IT IS NOT A CLAIM THAT THESE BYTES ARE DEBUG INFO, and the distinction is load-bearing: `strip` must not be able to remove the link-time optimizer's input. The `SectionKind` is its own role for exactly that reason. Its OWN SEGMENT `__DSS` -- the `__LLVM,__bitcode` precedent -- so the pair never lands inside a segment ld64 lays out. PAIRED with the `__mir` row below; the SPLIT is the whole economy (see section_kind.hpp).
sections.name: __summary

sections.$comment: D-LK-OBJECT-CARRIES-NO-SUMMARY-OR-MIR-SECTION. The module's serialized MIR body -- the LARGE half of the pair, read only for the modules the summary pass selected. Same segment and S_ATTR_DEBUG declaration as the summary row above and for the same reasons; the two differ in PAYLOAD, never in wire treatment.
sections.name: __mir

relocations.$comment: 32-bit PC-relative call/jmp. r_type = X86_64_RELOC_BRANCH (2), r_pcrel = 1, r_length = 2 (4 bytes). Mach-O `relocation_info.r_info` packs bits 28..31=r_type, 27=r_extern, 25..26=r_length, 24=r_pcrel, 0..23=r_symbolnum. The walker emits the static portion of r_info from this nativeId (type+length+pcrel = 0x25000000) and ORs in r_extern + r_symbolnum at emit time. `kind` = 1 matches x86_64.target.json's `rel32`. Mach-O has no Rela addend column — addends live in the patch bytes (the assembler writes 0; the linker computes target_va - (rip_after) - 0 since BRANCH is rip-relative). ★ `isCall` (D-LK-MACHO-ISDATA-NO-CALL-SIGNAL, 2026-08-20): this wire relocation can ONLY target executable code, so an object reader that meets an undefined extern through it has PROVEN the extern is a function rather than a data object -- the only classification signal a symbol-name-only reference offers. It is declared HERE, on the format row, and not derived from the target's formula, because a formula describes ARITHMETIC and not ROLE: `S + A - P` is the identical arithmetic for a call and for a PC-relative data reference, so the x86_64 target's `linear` is honest and simply carries no role, while aarch64's `aarch64_call26` looked like a role only because that CPU's branch has its own instruction encoding. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-20: every macho64-x86_64 archive member calling any library function was unreadable for exactly this reason while the arm64 sibling read the same source cleanly. The target document cannot carry it -- it is PER-CPU and shared with ELF, where the same `rel32` genuinely serves data references too.
relocations.name: X86_64_RELOC_BRANCH

relocations.$comment: Absolute 64-bit. r_type = X86_64_RELOC_UNSIGNED (0), r_pcrel = 0, r_length = 3 (8 bytes). nativeId = (0<<28)|(3<<25)|(0<<24) = 0x06000000. `kind` = 2 matches x86_64.target.json's `abs64`.
relocations.name: X86_64_RELOC_UNSIGNED_8

relocations.$comment: Absolute 32-bit. r_type = X86_64_RELOC_UNSIGNED (0), r_pcrel = 0, r_length = 2 (4 bytes). nativeId = (0<<28)|(2<<25)|(0<<24) = 0x04000000. `kind` = 3 matches x86_64.target.json's `abs32`.
relocations.name: X86_64_RELOC_UNSIGNED_4
